text: {"domains":{"block_M":[16,32,64,128],"block_N":[32,64,128,256],"block_K":[32,64,128],"num_stages":[1,2,3,4],"threads":[64,128,256],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16,32,64]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1,"launches":1,"pipeline":1,"footprint":1},"rationale":"Attempt-00 baseline (128x64x64, stage=1, threads=256, swizzle=0) ran ~3560.55 us with 766.5 MB DRAM and 2 blocks/SM. Attempt-02 (32x256x32, stage=1, threads=256, swizzle=64) improved to ~3518.99 us and roughly halved simulated DRAM to 450.9 MB, consistent with panel reuse helping; a schema ValueError in attempt-01 is fixed by keeping the full required JSON shape with all domains nonempty. Domains keep the expanded M/N/K tiles and stages 1-4 (as instructed) and full swizzle set; the 32768 cap plus the estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages,4*block_M*block_N) prunes oversized combos. Weights stay uniform since evidence is too thin to favor traffic, launches, pipeline, or footprint. Thread counts tie analytically for identical tile/stage/swizzle, so this round tests the changed thread/block_K hypothesis alongside swizzle>0 to see whether locality gains persist and whether larger block_K or stage=4 reduce pipeline cost. Scope: Metal checks simulate exact source/config/TIR; CUDA binaries are not executed, and GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements. Next hypothesis: pick a distinct tile/stage/thread combination (e.g. block_K=128, stage>=2) to test whether the reuse proxy's DRAM savings translate into lower simulated latency rather than just lower traffic."}
